newsitem.title: USA: Intl cotton group pegs 97/8 world crop at 19.1 MMT.
newsitem.headline: Intl cotton group pegs 97/8 world crop at 19.1 MMT.

text.p: The International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC) pegged 1997/98 world cotton output at 19.1 million tonnes, down 300,000 tonnes from the 1996/97 estimate and 130,000 tonnes below ICAC's forecast last month.

"Unusually wet and cool weather in parts of the USA, Pakistan, and Central Asia, a weak beginning to the monsoon in India, dry weather in North China (Mainland) and concerns about the possibility of drought in Australia and Southern Africa are leading to unease over the outlook for 1997/98 production..." the international cotton group said in its monthly report.

ICAC shaved its forecast for the U.S. crop by 100,000 tonnes to 3.9 million tonnes. It said India cotton production was expected to decline 200,000 tonnes to 2.6 million tonnes because of reduced area, but higher yields and production were expected in Pakistan, Uzbekistan and Turkey.
El Nino was raising concerns for production prospects in South India, Australia and Southern Africa, the group said, because of the increased possibility of drought.
The group also said with lower imports assumed for China in 1997/98, world trade was expected to decline to 5.9 million tonnes from 6.1 million tonnes in 1996/97.
